title: OS Command Injection
description: Command injection occurs when untrusted input is incorporated into an operating-system command without proper validation or neutralization.
impact: An attacker may execute unauthorized operating-system commands, access sensitive information, modify files, or compromise the host system.
common_causes: Building operating-system commands using string concatenation
Passing untrusted user input directly to command execution functions
mitigation: Pass commands as argument lists instead of shell command strings
Use absolute executable paths where appropriate

title: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code
description: Code injection occurs when attacker-controlled data is evaluated as executable programming language code.
impact: An attacker may execute arbitrary application code and potentially gain complete control over the application process.
common_causes: Using exec() on dynamically supplied input
Dynamically evaluating strings as Python code
mitigation: Avoid eval() and exec() with untrusted input
Use ast.literal_eval() when evaluating trusted literal data
Use structured data formats instead of executable strings

title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
description: Unsafe deserialization occurs when an application reconstructs objects from untrusted serialized data without sufficient validation.
impact: An attacker may execute arbitrary code, manipulate application state, or cause denial of service depending on the serialization mechanism.
common_causes: Deserializing objects received from untrusted sources
mitigation: Do not deserialize untrusted pickle data
Prefer JSON or other safe data formats
Use strict schemas for incoming data
Only deserialize trusted data from controlled sources

title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
description: Hardcoded credentials occur when passwords, API keys, tokens, or other secrets are embedded directly in application source code.
impact: Attackers who obtain the source code may recover credentials and gain unauthorized access to systems or services.
common_causes: API keys stored directly in source files
Database credentials embedded in application code
Authentication tokens embedded directly in application source code
mitigation: Never commit secrets to source control
Use different credentials for development and production
